newsitem.title: INDIA: India to offer fiscal incentives to telecom firms.
newsitem.headline: India to offer fiscal incentives to telecom firms.

text.p: India will treat telecommunications companies as infrastructure providers and offer them a tax holiday in their initial years as well as import duty concessions, the Finance Ministry said on Thursday.
Telecommunication companies will also be entitled to higher external borrowing limits, the ministry said in a statement.

"Telecom will be treated as infrastructure and all fiscal benefits like tax holiday, concessional project import duty etc., now being made available to the power sector will be extended to the telecom sector also," the statement said.
India, which began wooing foreign investors in the infrastructure industry under an economic reform programme launched in 1991, currently offers a uniform 20 percent import duty on power equipment.
Power generation companies also enjoy an exemption from income tax for the first five years and 30 percent of their profits are exempted from taxation for an additional five years.

Last year, India began awarding licences to private telecommunication companies to set up basic telephone services, ending a decades-old state monopoly. Several private mobile telephone companies are already operating in the country.
